nonclaim: This plan freezes one R33 V3 comparison collection over three externally assigned exclusive gfx942 hardware slots and external Ferric, vLLM, and SGLang lifecycle adapters. Measure adapters must return ordered per-request arrival, first-token, terminal, and token-work events; adapter reports remain observations, not independently validated facts. The collector does not validate tuning fairness, server freshness, slot exclusivity, hardware identity, model answers, numerical or hardware correctness, performance qualification, or independent reproduction, and it does not close m1.r33 or M1.

schema.commands: One policy-bound benchmark executable supplies separately identity-bound start, ready, measure, and stop argument vectors for each engine. The inherited environment is cleared. A bounded frozen environment plus reserved FERRIC_M1_R33_* bindings names the exact policy, action, command, engine, cyclic order, start, hardware slot, server instance, and window work. Nonzero exit, stderr, timeout, oversized output, noncanonical JSON, or binding drift aborts without publication.
schema.lifecycle: Each of three start ordinals starts and readies Ferric, vLLM, and SGLang on three distinct pre-frozen gfx942 slots with one byte-equal hardware-configuration identity. Engine-to-slot assignment rotates once per start. The returned server-instance identity is stable through that engine/start and distinct across all nine assignments. A canonical start result with a valid server-instance identity makes that assignment stoppable before the remaining result bindings are validated. Every applicable stop adapter is attempted in reverse order on success or failure even when input custody has drifted, and any custody or stop failure prevents publication. A start adapter that fails before returning a canonical valid server-instance identity is responsible for its own transactional cleanup. These identities are externally reported observations and do not independently establish freshness, exclusivity, hardware equivalence, or hardware identity.
schema.measurement: Each start contains ten ordered warmup windows followed by ten ordered recorded windows. Every row invokes three measurement children sequentially in the V3 cyclic engine order. The pre-execution roster fixes positive successful-request, input-token, output-token, and checked total-token work for each aligned row. Every engine must report exactly that work, zero failures, a positive declared-window duration, and one exact-key ordered event per successful request. Each event must use monotonic-raw-nanoseconds window-relative offsets with arrival < first token < terminal <= duration, positive input work, and at least two output tokens so TPOT is defined. Event token sums must equal window counters.
schema.output: The collector recomputes per-window nearest-rank p50, p90, and p99 E2E, TTFT, and TPOT from retained request events, constructs the exact FERRIC-M1-R33-SERVING-COMPARISON-OBSERVATIONS-V3 document, invokes the V3 structural and arithmetic validator, and publishes through its descriptor-held no-replace path. The final comparison record and performance gate remain a separate command.
schema.slots: Real collection requires three simultaneously exclusive MI300X-class gfx942:xnack- slots with distinct frozen hardware identities and one byte-equal hardware-configuration identity. The policy's server-start-roster SHA-256 is recomputed over the exact slots and all three rotated engine assignments. This protocol provides no HTTP server, launcher, allocation service, default engine configuration, or synthetic measurement path.
